title: Consistent hashing

kcs.statement: With hash(key) mod N placement, changing N from 4 to 5 moves about 80% of keys, because a key stays only when both remainders agree.
Consistent hashing places nodes and keys on the same hash ring and assigns each key to the first node clockwise from the key's position.
Adding or removing one node on a hash ring moves only the keys in that node's arc, about 1/N of all keys.
A ring lookup binary-searches the sorted node positions for the first position at or after the key's hash, wrapping to the first position when the hash is past the last one.
